courses.title: History of Hong Kong
courses.faculty: Faculty of Health and Social Sciences
courses.objectives: This course focuses on Hong Kong’s history from 1841 to 1997, covering issues in culture, politics, society, and economics. It aims to show how history explains the present while conveying the idea that historical interpretations continually evolve. Students will be encouraged to observe how interpretations of historical events stem from observers’ preconceptions and historical positions, and that historical facts acquire meaning only in relation to historical questions.
courses.summary: The course emphasizes: focusing on Hong Kong’s history from 1842 to 1997, covering issues in culture, politics, society, and economics. Teaching mode: primarily lecture-based, closely following assigned readings; students must complete pre-class reading assignments.
learningOutcomes: Understand that this course focuses on Hong Kong’s history from 1842 to 1997, covering issues in culture, politics, society, and economics.

Understand that this course not only addresses what happened in the past but also cultivates relevant competencies by teaching the following topics analytically and critically, using diverse sources to express varied perspectives.

Understand: 1. Introduction; 2. The opium trade during the early colonial period; 3. Establishment of the colonial system; 4. Rise of the Chinese elite; 5. Daily life in the pre-war period; 6. Hong Kong’s fall and Japanese occupation; 7. Post-war social and economic transformation: trading port, manufacturing hub, and financial center; 8. East-West convergence: the world of Soo Wong; 9. Reunification with the motherland.
Understand the teaching mode: primarily lecture-based, closely following assigned readings; students must complete pre-class reading assignments.

courses.title: Modern and Contemporary Chinese History and Culture
courses.objectives: This course aims to provide new perspectives on the relationship between cultural texts and concrete historical issues, situating them within a global context. Through interdisciplinary and multimedia approaches, the course seeks to present emotional, aesthetic, and sensory experiences of twentieth-century China, covering multiple genres and media to enable students to gain diverse experiences of modern Chinese history. Thus, this course will help students develop a deeper understanding of modern Chinese history and culture and enrich their ways of experiencing the world.
courses.summary: This course introduces important themes from the early 20th century to the present, covering China's position in war, Mao Zedong's revolutionary culture and the Cultural Revolution, the reform and opening-up policy and its impact on daily life, the rise of the middle class culture, and issues related to migrant workers and developmentalism.
